t: The Best Time To Review Your Classroom Management Plan
q: No, the best time to review your classroom management plan is . . . When everything is going perfectly.
By revisiting your behavior expectations out of the blue , as well as the precise boundary lines that protect learning, you send the message that you’re the same consistent teacher day after day.
A surprise lesson on classroom management, when things are going so well and no teacher in the world would do the same, keeps misbehavior far from shore.
Taking the extra step, when good enough is the cultural norm, is something only those who pursue excellence ever do.
Great teachers are outliers. They’re independent thinkers. They’re rebels as well as rule followers.
For those students, for those you have only a short window in a lifetime to make an impact, to inspire and set firmly on a path of contribution and empathy for others . . . It means everything.

t: How To Fix A Talkative Class
q: The truth is, you can fix excessive and impermissible talking and expect silence whenever you need it.
You must change the culture of sloppiness and carelessness first before you can expect to rid your classroom of chattiness, side-whispering, and the like.
There must be complete understanding of what silence is according to your definition before you can ask them to replicate it.
They need to know that the ability to concentrate for long periods of time is a critical success skill that is key to their learning, their progress, and their very future.
They’re not allowed to speak to the offending party, look at them, or make any other gesture. They just hold up their signal and continue working.
Restore respect for you and every student in the class by defending their right to learn and enjoy school without interference .

q: No single area of teaching comes remotely close to providing the joy, the peace, and the effectiveness every teacher desires.
They are the small cadre of experts that leap out of bed in the morning and grow bored during the summer months.
They assume that it’s just how things are or buy into the myth that their problems lie with the students, parents, school, or administration.
You have to stop bribing students, trying to convince them to behave, or believing that you just have a chatty bunch—as if you’re at their mercy.
If you put what you learn into practice, and remain consistent, you’ll not only see stunning results almost immediately, but you’ll be on your way to the long, happy career you’ve always wanted.
x: Frames classroom management as the single area of teaching most responsible for a teacher's joy, peace, and effectiveness.

q: Four of every ten new teachers leave the profession within five years.
This is by far the most important thing you can do to begin enjoying your job. When students are well-behaved and attentive, everything is easier.
It can be hard to say no, especially if you’re a new teacher eager to please.
According the American Federation of Teachers, 61 percent of teachers say their work is always or often stressful.
You don’t have to be a martyr who sacrifices health and happiness for your students, parents, principal, school, society, or anyone else.
But you do have to fight back. You do have to be determined.
